bullets: Define two classes: class I and Class II
let d(X) be a discriminant function = W^T X
if X ∈ class I then d(X) > 0
if X ∈ class II then d(X) < 0
If X ∈ class I and misclassified as Class II then d(X) will be <0
If X ∈ class II and misclassified as Class I then d(X) will be >0
Error = Σ_{all misclassified vectors(i)} (W^T X_i) ⇒ (W^T X_i) take positive and negative values
If X ∈ class I and misclassified as Class II then d(X) will be <0 ⇒ δ_i = -1 ⇒ d(X) δ_i >0
If X ∈ class II and misclassified as Class I then d(X) will be >0 ⇒ δ_i = +1 ⇒ d(X) δ_i >0

recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to white. Add the title Problem Formulation at the top-center in bold red #C00000, large sans-serif. 2. Add a yellow #FFFF00 circle with a thin black outline at the top-right and place the black bold text 36 centered inside it. 3. Add four full-width rectangles from about x=3% to x=97%, stacked vertically with small gaps. Give each a dark red #A60000 border and a very light gray #F7F7F7 fill. Use left-aligned text with comfortable inner padding. 4. In the first box, place: Define two classes: class I and Class II / let d(X) be a discriminant function = W^T X / if X ∈ class I then d(X) > 0 / if X ∈ class II then d(X) < 0. Color class I green #008000 and Class II blue #0000FF; keep d(X) red #C00000 and the inequality results blue #0000FF. 5. In the second box, place: For misclassified X : / If X ∈ class I and misclassified as Class II then d(X) will be <0 / If X ∈ class II and misclassified as Class I then d(X) will be >0. Underline misclassified, color class I green and Class II blue, and keep the inequality results blue. 6. In the third box, place the heading Define Error function as: with Error underlined. Center the equation Error = Σ_{all misclassified vectors(i)} (W^T X_i) ⇒ (W^T X_i) take positive and negative values. Make the summation subscript and the explanatory phrase red #C00000, and add a large red #FF0000 X at the far right of the box. 7. In the fourth box, place: Define δ_i as : with δ_i underlined. Then add the two conditional lines exactly: If X ∈ class I and misclassified as Class II then d(X) will be <0 ⇒ δ_i = -1 ⇒ d(X) δ_i >0 and If X ∈ class II and misclassified as Class I then d(X) will be >0 ⇒ δ_i = +1 ⇒ d(X) δ_i >0. Use red #C00000 for the implication arrows and δ_i assignments, blue #0000FF for the final >0 results, green #008000 for class I, and blue #0000FF for Class II.
